what: Claude Fable 5.1's test-retest duel agreement on lot A was stated as 91.7 %; it is 90.0 % (9 of 10 duels).
why: The lab's count had taken code-review verdicts (yes / partly / no) for duels and counted each duel twice; the corrected count still meets the gate's 90 % threshold.

what: The duel criteria of the lot-A judge gate were labelled 'same duel winner' until 2026-10-02; they are now labelled 'same duel verdict (a winner, a tie, or incoherent)'.
why: The lab's rule has compared duel verdicts, an incoherent duel included, since before GPT-6 Astra graded lot A; the old label described the strict reading instead, under which the gate would not pass (cross_checks[id=cloud-lot-a].inter_family.strict_reading_passes). Both readings are now published.

what: The medical-imaging aggregate scores published in v0 (the two aggregate scores per model, each with its 95 % interval, of MedGemma 1.5 4B and the RADAR reference on the imagerie-med/v1 bench, and the order of the two models) are withdrawn: the imaging ranking is removed and the MedGemma run no longer carries a quality entry.
why: A precaution about the data-use agreement of the dataset behind these measurements (Merlin, Stanford AIMI): since 2026-10-03, medical-imaging scores are withheld until the data-use agreement's publication clause has been reviewed. Nothing per exam was ever published.

what: Ranks and tie groups in the 2026-10-01 tutoring and agentic-code tables changed when the row of Qwen3.8-27B (EXL3 3.21 bpw, OrcaSAQ-2), graded after v0, was added: in tutoring every row from OxCoder-9B down moved down one place; in code Gemma 4 26B-A4B moved from 5th to 6th, Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B from 8th to 7th, Nex-N2.5-mini (W4A16) from 6th to 8th, NeoHorse-1-9B from 7th to 9th, OxCoder-9B from 9th to 10th (no longer in a tie group) and every row below it down one place; the code table's robustness figures moved (τ 0.933 to 0.957, first 10 rows 0.867 to 0.956, places changed 12 to 9; tutoring places changed 14 to 15).
why: An addition, not a correction: the run had been shown as not graded by the table's judge yet; its Claude Fable 5.1 grades (2026-10-03) give it a rank like every other row, which moves the rows below it.

what: The headline speed figures (single-stream and eight-request throughput, time to first token, ready time and the after-load memory snapshot) of 17 model rows now come from 17 of the 18 runs of the 2026-10-03 speed campaign: on one card Gemma 4 26B-A4B, NeoHorse-1-9B, Spark-X2.5-4B GGUF, Granite 4.2 3B, Qwen3.8-9B-Distill, OxCoder-9B GGUF and NeoHorse-1-4B GGUF; on the NVLink pair Gemma 4 26B-A4B, Qwen3.8-27B W4A16, Thomson-1.0-Small, Qwen3.6-27B-Fable-Fusion-711, Gemma 4 31B, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GGUF, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B, Muse Glimmer 30B GGUF, Gemma 3 27B QAT and Qwen3.8-27B Cold-Fusion. Six of the earlier headlines were pre-pin runs and one a speculative-decoding-protocol run (spec-ab/v1). The largest moves: Thomson-1.0-Small 173.9 → 159.5 tok/s single stream and 985.8 → 902.4 at eight (the earlier run on vLLM 0.26.0, the new one on 0.29.0 with the same engine arguments; the cause was not isolated); Qwen3.8-27B Cold-Fusion 396.6 → 528.7 at eight; Gemma 4 26B-A4B on the pair 1004.2 (spec-ab/v1) → 1118.4 at eight; Spark-X2.5-4B GGUF 116.0 → 112.3 single stream and 117.1 → 113.2 at eight.
why: An addition, not a correction: the 2026-10-03 runs (pinned engine, house protocol, most recent) take the headline under the unchanged rule (methodology/headline-rule.md); the earlier runs and their figures are unchanged and listed beside them. MiniCPM5-2B keeps its 2026-09-13 headline, whose speed pass was repeated three times.
